newsitem.title: USA: Florida governor deposed in state's tobacco case.
newsitem.headline: Florida governor deposed in state's tobacco case.

text.p: Florida Gov. Lawton Chiles answered questions Wednesday on his experiences with cigarettes and his personal investments in preparation for the state's lawsuit against tobacco companies.

Chiles, whose state is seeking damages from cigarette makers to recoup the Medicaid costs of treating smoking-related illnesses, was deposed for nearly five hours as the two sides prepared for the trial, scheduled to begin August 1.
"They've asked me everything from when I was born to the time I was in state Legislature to when I was in Congress," Chiles said as he returned for the afternoon round of questions.
"They've asked if I made any inconsistent votes on tobacco during my career. Things like that," he said.
An ex-smoker, Chiles was asked to recount his own smoking experiences during the deposition, which began at 0900 EDT/1300 GMT. He was also questioned about his personal investments.
"I can't think of anything they haven't asked me," said Chiles, who expects to be called as a witness at the trial.
Chiles is one of number of high-ranking officials and industry executives scheduled to be deposed over the next few weeks.
Louis Camilleri, chief financial officer for Philip Morris Cos Inc was scheduled to be deposed this weekend, said Tim Howard, a Tallahassee attorney coordinating the state's case.
Depositions of top cigarette industry officials, including Philip Morris Chief Executive Geoffrey Bible, are set for August.
In West Palm Beach Wednesday, the Florida Fourth District Court of Appeals ruled the state could use internal tobacco company documents as evidence in the trial.
